title: 1:1 Preflight — PM ↔ Eng Lead (API/Dedicated) — Samira
body:
Purpose
- Quick sync with Eng Lead to align on short-term priorities across Hosted API + Dedicated pools. Prep so we use the 30m efficiently: unblock, decide on canary window, agree on owners for follow-ups.

Context / TL;DR
- p95 generation latency for small-chat models spiked on 2026-02-26 after kernel selection change (approx +40ms).
- Dedicated pool utilization steady (~87%) but tail latency impact causing some customer complaints (CS ticket cluster).
- Cost per 1k tokens improved slightly after quantization move but need to validate quality regressions.

Top agenda (30m)
1) Quick data check (5m): confirm metrics and current hypothesis for root cause.
2) Short-term mitigation (10m): decide rollback vs targeted canary, fallback policies for affected routes.
3) Dedicated pool ops (7m): capacity/burst plan and SLA communication for customers impacted.
4) Action items & owners (8m).

Notes to self (pre-meeting)
- Bring these numbers: p50/p95/p99 for API-chat-small over last 7 days, error rate trend (0.2% -> 0.8%), percent of requests hitting fallback (3%).
- Have link to the perf-run comparing kernels (confluence link above).
- Prepare short script: how to toggle kernel A/B in canary (Ethan wrote it).

Hypotheses (for discussion)
- H1: New kernel selection picks a slower matmul path for short sequences due to heuristic misclassification.
- H2: Continuous batching config changed default max_wait_ms leading to slightly larger batches causing queuing at tail during spike.
- H3: KV cache invalidation bug causing extra mem copies on dedicated hosts (low probability but needs check).

Quick mitigations to propose
- Immediate: revert kernel selection change for canary routes (low blast radius), enable emergency fallback to older model variant for SLO-critical customers.
- Near-term: push updated batching config (reduce max_wait_ms) to affected clusters for 2-4h window and monitor.
- Medium: run offline kernel selection simulation with live trace to validate heuristics.

Questions for Eng Lead (priority order)
1) If we rollback kernel change to canary only, how quickly can we roll back prod if canary looks good? (ETA?)
2) Do we have enough Dedicated spare capacity to route SLO-critical customers to dedicated-only endpoints for the next 48h?
3) Risk/impact of toggling batching config live (will it affect throughput/backpressure across tenants?)
4) Any known changes in infra (memory/driver versions) coincident with 2026-02-26?
5) Are there outstanding PRs touching KV cache that should be held?

Decisions I want to land in this 1:1
- Agree rollback approach vs canary expansion (binary decision).
- Assign owner for Customer comms for impacted customers (email + incident postmortem template).
- Confirm who will own the postmortem and target delivery date.

Proposed action items (post-meeting)
- Action A: "Canary rollback plan" — Owner: Ethan M. — Due: 2026-03-14 — Steps: run canary revert, monitor p95 for 60m, if stable promote to prod.
- Action B: "Dedicated routing for SLO customers" — Owner: Jordan L. — Due: 2026-03-13 — Steps: update routing policy, validate connectivity and costs, flag customers.
- Action C: "Batching config test" — Owner: Samira P. (PM) + Eng — Due: 2026-03-16 — Steps: run controlled A/B with reduced max_wait_ms, observe throughput/loss.
- Action D: "Postmortem draft" — Owner: Samira P. — Due: 2026-03-20 — Collect timelines, customer impact, root cause.

Customer/CS notes to mention
- CS: 4 tickets from enterprise accounts referencing slow responses during 2026-02-26 window. Need prioritized comms.
- Suggested comms: short note acknowledging investigation, ETA for mitigation, offer to route to older model variant for the most impacted customers.

Escalation plan (if rollback fails)
- Move to emergency meeting with SRE and infra leads -> trace level increase, rollback at host/driver level if needed, possibly throttle non-critical routes.
- Exec notify if >3 major customers impacted after 24h.

Follow-ups I will do before meeting
- Drop perf graphs into the doc, attach a short runnable playbook for canary revert (copy Ethan's gist).
- Ping SRE for quick sanity check on driver/OS changes last week.

Random notes / backlog items to briefly surface if time
- Dedicated: plan for burst capacity pricing model — status? (Product ops ask)
- Console: add per-route kernel toggle in the rollout UI (low effort, high observational value).
- Optimize: run eval on quantized checkpoints for a random small prompt set to detect quality drift.

Reminders to self (meeting etiquette)
- Start with 1 quick win (acknowledge Eng work on quantization) then move to blockers.
- Keep decisions timeboxed — pick either canary or rollback; avoid open-ended analysis in the 1:1.

End of doc.
